titleSelected: Roman Concrete Could Heal Its Own Cracks
titleAlternate: The 'Mistakes' That Made Roman Concrete Stronger

editorial.viewerQuestion: How could ancient Roman concrete seal its own cracks?
editorial.finalLesson: Researchers propose that reactive lime clasts created by hot mixing could dissolve when water entered a crack and recrystallize as calcium carbonate; Roman-inspired laboratory samples healed cracks up to 0.5 millimetres within two weeks while controls did not.
editorial.evidenceLimit: The mechanism is supported by material analysis and a modern Roman-inspired test, but it does not show that every Roman structure used the same recipe or that all Roman concrete literally self-healed in every condition.
editorial.hook: Did you know Roman concrete may have repaired its own cracks?
editorial.payoff: The features once dismissed as sloppy white 'mistakes' may have been part of the durable hot-mixing design.
